actual_scope: One named current condition of the selected-bit supplier's compact dirty-control operation (notes/compact-control-movement.tex, 'Guards and deterministic repair'): the exact raw agreement-and-restoration set of the earlier-source and later-source routines, computed on complete bounded domains (n in {2,3}, K in {3,4,5,6}, G in {1,2}, 47 cells, 24,074,240 fiber states) and compared with the published sufficient guards G0 (source note), G1 (research/compact-carry-repair-audit) and H (research/compact-late-guard-audit-seed73). Independent sufficiency check of all three guards plus smallest semantic counterexamples to their necessity.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one named current obligation traced through its source-bound checks, with an allowed variation of auditing one named condition using a new semantic counterexample. Refined from the card's generic wording to this specific condition: the sampled acceptance of the packed selected-bit operation (docs/audit.md records only 4,500 sampled triples) left the exact agreement set uncharacterized, and research/compact-late-guard-audit-seed73 explicitly states its guard is not the global exact agreement set. The card's premise (audit one supplier obligation; no construction) is unchanged.
bottleneck_link: Source-bound reliability of the selected bit supplier's exceptional-repair/restoration condition. A repair envelope priced on the true agreement set rather than a sufficient guard would reduce exceptional-repair work; no kappa or packing-cap change is claimed and the a < D/E and whole-construction budgets do not apply to an audit.
stop_rule: One bounded pivot maximum; kill any route whose optimistic budget misses the target. Stop when one named condition is audited with complete-domain evidence, positive fixtures and failure controls, or when the smallest falsifying instance is recorded. No kappa target is set for this audit.
evidence: research/compact-agreement-set-seed29/verify.py (independent stdlib interpreter and census), RESULT.json (receipt: 24,074,240 states; 11,880,712 raw agreements; 47 cells), README.md. Sufficiency of G0/G1/H holds on every enumerated cell (zero violations); the exact agreement set strictly exceeds every guard everywhere (49.35% overall versus guard maxima 14.06%/7.03%/44.83%); seed73's closed form (2) matches the enumerated H counts exactly at all 21 later-source cells; both published failure fixtures (16,4224,0,1,2 and 2,124,1,0,7) reproduce exactly; mutated-unloading and spectatorship controls behave as required.
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: task selection, transcription, implementation, verification and writing were done with help from opencode. Contributor: Aaron Wang.

open_questions.question: Characterize the exact raw agreement set AG structurally: which states outside every digit-local guard are nevertheless exactly correct, and is a digit-local predicate possible at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A repair envelope priced on AG rather than a sufficient guard would shrink the exceptional-repair workload the scan and radix sort must pay for.
open_questions.first_step: Classify the AG \ H states at n=2,K=4,G=1 by which guard clause fails (never-loaded saturation vs systematic source-dependent region) and test any proposed predicate on the next geometry.
open_questions.blocked_by: No computational blocker; a plausible predicate form is the missing ingredient.
